verdict: Yes, if you start with home visits and buy a van only once your calendar is full. Pet owners in Indian cities pay well for doorstep grooming and rebook every four to six weeks. The van is where most founders go wrong: its monthly loan payment only pays off at four to six grooms a day, and traffic makes that hard.
angle: Doorstep grooming suits anxious pets and busy owners, and apartment communities spread recommendations quickly. Shark Tank India saw a mobile pet grooming pitch in Season 1 (Flying Fur), and the questions were familiar: how many grooms a van does per day, and how you keep trained groomers. A founder who builds trust with a few hundred regular clients through vets and housing societies has a steady, cash-positive local business.

faq.q: How much does it cost to start mobile pet grooming?
faq.a: Home visits with a portable kit cost ₹1.5–3 lakh including training and insurance. A fitted grooming van with water, heating and power costs ₹12–25 lakh.

faq.q: How much can a pet groomer earn per groom?
faq.a: A full groom at home sells for ₹800–2,500 depending on the breed and coat. After consumables, travel and groomer pay, ₹450–700 per groom is typical before any van loan.

faq.q: Do I need a certificate to groom pets?
faq.a: There is no mandatory licence, but a professional grooming course and supervised practice are essential for safe handling and for earning owners' trust.

faq.q: How many grooms can a mobile van do in a day?
faq.a: In big-city traffic, four to six grooms a day is realistic if you group appointments by area.
